title: Buy Now, Maybe Pay Later: Dealing with Prompt-Tax While Staying at the Frontier - Andrew Thomspson
talk_summary: Tactics include stripping over-specified instructions for reasoning models, using the new model itself to migrate old prompts, and feature-flagging model upgrades.

takeaways.technique: Use the new model to migrate its own prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: When a new model lands, they feed the existing domain-specific prompts into the new model and have it rewrite/migrate them, instead of hand-editing hundreds of prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by feeding that domain specific prompt into the new model, it can help us migrate those uh prompts and radically uh decrease the amount of manual human effort
takeaways.numbers: grew from ~0 to well over 1,000 domain-specific prompts

takeaways.technique: Strip how-to and repetition for reasoning models
takeaways.what_they_do: For system-2/reasoning models they remove step-by-step instructions and repeated reminders, giving a clear objective and letting the model reason; keep those only for cheaper system-1 models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: With system two models, we didn't need to do that. We needed to strip all that out and just specify what to do.

takeaways.technique: Feature-flag model upgrades with progressive rollout
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat model version changes like feature flags: roll out internally first, then to a slice of users, scaling up as feedback volume stays manageable, dialing back if it swamps the team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: rolling this out internally first, then to a limited number of sort of progressive users and scaling that up to 50 or 100% of users over time

takeaways.technique: Fast human/domain-expert feedback loop into prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: In-product thumbs feedback routes immediately to a domain expert who edits the prompt and ships it to production, fixing it for all users within minutes to hours.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that domain expert evaluates it, figures out what prompt needs to get changed, makes that change and then ships that into production
takeaways.numbers: fix cycles of minutes or hours vs days or weeks

takeaways.technique: Vibes-plus-spreadsheet regression tracking as a stopgap
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately ship on subjective expert review plus lightweight spreadsheet logging of regressions instead of a full eval suite, acknowledging it may not scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've come all this way in 18 months on pretty much vibes alone

takeaways.technique: Cheap system-1 models for sub-tasks, reasoning models where needed
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep using cheaper/faster system-1 models for many subtasks and reserve system-2 reasoning models for hard planning, using thought tokens for debugging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: system one models can be really helpful. They're often cheaper. They're often faster.
